fact: T-Rex had the strongest bite of any land animal ever — about 12,800 pounds of force! That's like having a small car dropped on you.
Velociraptors were actually only about the size of a turkey, not the giant creatures shown in movies!
The Argentinosaurus was so massive it weighed about 100 tons — that's heavier than 14 African elephants combined!
Stegosaurus had a brain the size of a walnut, but it had bony plates on its back that could flush with blood to regulate body temperature.
Pterodactyls weren't actually dinosaurs! They were flying reptiles called pterosaurs that lived alongside dinosaurs.
The name 'dinosaur' means 'terrible lizard' in Greek — but dinosaurs weren't actually lizards at all!
Spinosaurus is the largest known carnivorous dinosaur, even bigger than T-Rex! It was also a fantastic swimmer.
Triceratops' frill wasn't just for protection — scientists think it was used to attract mates, like a peacock's tail!
Some dinosaurs swallowed stones called gastroliths to help grind up food in their stomachs, kind of like how birds use grit today!
The Ankylosaurus had a tail club so powerful it could break the bones of a T-Rex. Talk about a built-in weapon!
Dinosaurs lived on every continent, including Antarctica! Back then, it was covered in forests, not ice.
The Micropachycephalosaurus has the longest name of any dinosaur — try saying that five times fast!
Birds are technically dinosaurs! They evolved from small theropod dinosaurs and are the only dinosaur lineage that survived the extinction.
Parasaurolophus had a long hollow crest on its head that it could use like a trumpet to make deep, booming sounds!
The asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs was about 6 miles wide — roughly the size of Mount Everest!
Brachiosaurus could eat leaves from trees up to 30 feet high — that's like eating off the roof of a three-story building!
Some dinosaur eggs were as big as footballs! The largest ever found belonged to a type of oviraptorosaur.
Compsognathus was one of the smallest dinosaurs — about the size of a chicken! But it was a fierce little predator.
The Utahraptor was the largest raptor dinosaur, about 23 feet long and 1,100 pounds. Now THAT's a raptor!
Dinosaurs dominated Earth for about 165 million years. Humans have only been around for about 300,000 years!
Pachycephalosaurus had a skull dome 10 inches thick! Scientists debate whether they head-butted each other like rams.
The Quetzalcoatlus had a wingspan of 36 feet — as wide as a small airplane! It was the largest flying animal ever.
Therizinosaurus had claws up to 3 feet long — the longest claws of any animal that ever lived!
The first dinosaur fossil ever scientifically described was Megalosaurus in 1824, by William Buckland in England.
Diplodocus could crack its tail like a whip, creating a sonic boom that could be heard from miles away!
Some scientists believe T-Rex had feathers — at least as a baby. Imagine a fluffy T-Rex chick!
Iguanodon was one of the first three dinosaurs ever named, and scientists originally put its thumb spike on its nose like a horn!
The Giganotosaurus from South America had a skull over 5 feet long — one of the biggest heads ever on a land predator!
Sauropod dinosaurs could grow so fast that some species gained up to 2 tons per year during their growth spurts!
Dreadnoughtus, meaning 'fears nothing', was one of the most massive land animals ever — weighing about 65 tons!
The Dilophosaurus had two distinctive crests on its head. Despite what Jurassic Park showed, there's no evidence it could spit venom!
Allosaurus was the top predator of the Jurassic period — 150 million years before T-Rex was even born!
The Carnotaurus had tiny, almost useless arms — even smaller in proportion than T-Rex's arms!
Mosasaurus wasn't a dinosaur — it was a giant marine lizard that ruled the ancient seas and grew up to 56 feet long!
Oviraptor's name means 'egg thief' — but it was wrongly accused! Scientists later found it was actually sitting on its OWN eggs.
The Baryonyx had a crocodile-like snout and hooked claws, perfectly designed for snatching fish from rivers.
Carcharodontosaurus, named after the great white shark, had serrated teeth and rivaled T-Rex in size!
Protoceratops fossils found in the Gobi Desert with Velociraptor bones show them locked in combat — frozen in time for 80 million years!
Kentrosaurus had sharp spikes running all the way down its back and tail — some spikes were over 2 feet long!
The Mammoth existed long AFTER the dinosaurs died — it lived alongside humans, who actually hunted it!
Psittacosaurus, the 'parrot lizard', had bristle-like quills on its tail — making it one of the spikiest small dinosaurs!
Plateosaurus was one of the first large dinosaurs. It could walk on all fours OR rear up on two legs to reach high leaves!
Edmontosaurus had thousands of teeth packed into its jaws — a 'dental battery' that could grind even the toughest plants.
Struthiomimus looked and ran like an ostrich! It could sprint at speeds of up to 50 mph — faster than any land predator.
The Microraptor had four wings — one pair on its arms and one on its legs! It glided through Cretaceous forests like a tiny biplane.
Corythosaurus had a hollow bony crest shaped like a half-moon. Like a natural instrument, it amplified its calls through the forest.
Maiasaura, the 'good mother lizard', is the first dinosaur proven to have raised and cared for its young in a nest!
T-Rex couldn't stick out its tongue! Like modern crocodiles, its tongue was attached flat to the bottom of its mouth.
Epidexipteryx was a tiny dinosaur with four long ribbon-like tail feathers — possibly used for display, just like a peacock!
Suchomimus had a thumb claw over a foot long — great for hooking fish right out of rivers!
A single Brachiosaurus needed to eat about 880 pounds of food every single day just to survive!
Fossil footprints (called trace fossils) can tell scientists how fast a dinosaur moved, and even if it travelled in groups!
The Cretaceous period ended 66 million years ago when a massive asteroid hit Chicxulub, Mexico — wiping out 75% of all life on Earth!
Some dinosaurs may have lived for over 300 years! Growth rings in bones, like tree rings, help scientists estimate their age.
Troodon had the largest brain relative to its body size of any known dinosaur — it may have been as smart as a modern bird!
The word 'fossil' comes from the Latin 'fossilis', meaning 'dug up'. Fossils can take millions of years to form!
Herrerasaurus was one of the earliest true dinosaurs, living about 230 million years ago during the Triassic period.
Mamenchisaurus had the longest neck of any dinosaur — up to 46 feet long! That's longer than a school bus!
The Coelacanth fish is sometimes called a 'living fossil' — it's almost unchanged from when dinosaurs were alive 65 million years ago!
Gallimimus ran in huge herds across open plains of Mongolia — a bit like the wildebeest migrations of today!
Sinosauropteryx was the first non-bird dinosaur found with fossilized feather impressions — a huge discovery in 1996!
The Irritator — a real dinosaur name! — was named after scientists' frustration when fossil dealers tampered with the skull before selling it.
Sauroposeidon may have been the tallest dinosaur ever, able to raise its head about 60 feet in the air — as tall as a six-story building!
Archaeopteryx, discovered in 1861, is one of the most famous fossils in history. It had both dinosaur teeth AND bird feathers!
Theropod dinosaurs — the group including T-Rex and Velociraptor — walked on two legs and mostly ate meat.
Liopleurodon was a massive marine reptile with jaws over 10 feet long — not a dinosaur, but definitely terrifying!
Styracosaurus had an elaborate frill with six long spikes radiating from it — one of the most spectacular heads in dinosaur history.
Velociraptors hunted in packs and used their sickle-shaped toe claw to slash and hold down prey — not to slash throats as movies show.
The Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods are all part of the Mesozoic Era — also called the 'Age of Reptiles'.
Albertosaurus, a relative of T-Rex, may have hunted in packs! A bone bed in Canada had over 26 individuals together.
The duck-billed dinosaurs (hadrosaurs) could have up to 1,400 teeth packed in their jaws — more than any other dinosaur!
Camarasaurus was the most common large sauropod in North America. Hundreds of its fossils have been found!
Some titanosaur sauropods had armour embedded in their skin — tiny bony studs called osteoderms for extra protection!
The Triassic extinction event 201 million years ago wiped out many species and cleared the way for dinosaurs to dominate!
Dinosaur skin impressions have been found in fossils! Some hadrosaurs had pebbly, bumpy skin — not scales like a snake.
Coelophysis was a slender, fast-running predator that lived in packs during the Late Triassic — one of the earliest dinosaurs!
The discovery of 'Sue', a 90% complete T-Rex skeleton found in 1990, sold at auction for $8.3 million dollars!
Spinosaurus likely walked on all four limbs for much of the time, especially when wading in rivers — unlike how movies portray it.
Saltasaurus, a titanosaur from Argentina, was one of the first sauropods discovered with armoured skin — a real surprise for scientists!
Some ornithopod dinosaurs, like Hypsilophodon, could run very fast on two legs to escape predators — reaching speeds of 25 mph!
Many theropod dinosaurs, including T-Rex, had hollow bones — just like modern birds. This made them lighter and faster!
Apatosaurus (once called Brontosaurus) was so large that its footsteps would have shaken the ground like a minor earthquake!
The Spinosaurus sail on its back could grow up to 6 feet tall — scientists still debate whether it was a sail, hump, or fin.
Amargasaurus had two rows of tall spines running down its neck and back — possibly covered in a sail of skin!
Ichthyosaurs looked just like dolphins but were actually reptiles that lived 250 million years ago — convergent evolution in action!
Stegosaurus and T-Rex never met! They lived 83 million years apart — closer in time to us than to each other.
The Jurassic Park/World franchise got Velociraptors totally wrong — the raptors in the movies are actually based on Deinonychus and Utahraptor!
Pachycephalosaurus had a dome-shaped skull that could be 10 times thicker than the skulls of other large dinosaurs.
China has become one of the richest places on Earth for feathered dinosaur fossils — reshaping everything we know about how birds evolved!
Argentinosaurus's vertebrae were so big that a person could stand inside one of them — they were over 5 feet tall!
Plesiosaurs weren't dinosaurs but marine reptiles with four large flippers and extremely long necks — inspiring legends of sea monsters!
Tyrannosaurids like T-Rex had scaly skin on their faces and possibly fleshy lips that covered their teeth — no more grinning skulls!
Deinonychus, discovered in 1964, completely changed how scientists viewed dinosaurs — it showed they were likely active, warm-blooded hunters!
The Troodon's eyes were huge and forward-facing, giving it excellent depth perception for night hunting — like a prehistoric owl!
Ankylosaurus was so armoured its eyelids were even protected by bony plates — practically a living tank!
The longest dinosaur name that's easy to pronounce is Bambiraptor — named after the Disney deer because of its small and graceful skeleton!
More dinosaur species have been discovered in the last 20 years than in the previous 100 years combined!
Some dinosaur fossils have been found with preserved soft tissues — including collagen and even traces of pigment cells!
Carnotaurus was so fast for its size that scientists estimate it could reach speeds of 35 mph — sprinting like a racehorse!
The Cretaceous period was so warm that palm trees grew inside the Arctic Circle and there was no ice at the poles!
Diplodocus was over 85 feet long but weighed only about 12 tons — much lighter than you'd expect for such a long animal!
Concavenator had a strange hump before its hips. Scientists think the hump may have stored fat for energy, like a camel!
Parasaurolophus' hollow crest could produce sound like a trombone — its resonating frequencies have been recreated by scientists!
Over 700 species of non-avian dinosaurs have been named so far — and scientists discover around 50 new species every single year!
Ouranosaurus had tall neural spines on its back that likely supported a sail, helping regulate body temperature in hot African climates.
The Nothronychus was a North American therizinosaur — a plant-eating theropod that looked like a giant, shaggy, clawed sloth!
Dinosaur bones have been found on every continent, including Antarctica — fossils of Cryolophosaurus were found near the South Pole!
T-Rex's tiny arms were actually very powerful — each could curl about 400 pounds. They may have helped it push up from the ground!
Yutyrannus, a feathered cousin of T-Rex from China, is the largest known feathered animal that ever existed — about 30 feet long!
Nanotyrannus is one of paleontology's biggest debates — some scientists think it's a young T-Rex, others think it's a totally different species!
